utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody. May I ask Madam Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. This is case number IT-98-29/1-A, the Prosecutor versus Dragomir Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you. May I have the appearances of the party for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEWIS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Nicole Lewis, appearing for the Prosecution, together with my co-counsel, Ms. Shelagh McCall, and our case manager, Mr. Sebastiaan van Hooydonk.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you. For the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. I'm attorney at law Branislav Tapuskovic, appearing for Dragomir Milosevic, and with me is my co-counsel, Branislava Isailovic, an attorney at law from Paris. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: I thank you. Now, may I turn to Mr. Milosevic, and may I ask you if you can hear and follow the proceedings in a language you understand .

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you. I can hear and understand everything. I can follow, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, this is a status conference called in accordance with Rule 65 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, which requires, as everybody knows, that a status conference be convened within 120 days from the filing of a notice of appeal and thereafter within, again, 120 days after the last status conference. The purpose of the status conference is, first, to allow any person in custody, pending an appeal, the opportunity to raise issues in relation to its detention. So may I first ask the counsel for the Defence if there is any question of this kind to be raised here? And then I will ask Mr. Milosevic himself. But, please, Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, to the best of my knowledge, observing the mental and physical health of Mr. Dragomir Milosevic, I think there are no complaints concerning the conditions in the Detention Unit of this Tribunal. He will certainly not raise any issues in that respect. However, he will address you now. He is expecting to learn quite soon the decision of your Chamber concerning his motion for provisional release for the reasons stated in the motion. There is nothing further for me to add, and of course Mr. Milosevic himself will inform you of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tapuskovic. May I ask Mr. Milosevic, himself, if he has any issue to raise concerning the detention, apart from the motion for provisional release that we will address later, but please, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. With respect to the conditions in the Detention Unit, I have no issues to raise, nor do I have anything to say concerning any possible problems. In brief, everything is in good order. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you may sit down. As to the question of the provisional release, on 14 April the Defence filed an application for provisional release pursuant to Rule 65(i), to which the Prosecution responded on 18 April. I can say only that the Appeals Chamber is currently dealing with the application, and I can anticipate that it will render a decision very soon. It's a question of days, maybe even tomorrow or the day after tomorrow we can issue the decision. So it's a question of a very short time in which the Appeal Chamber will render its decision. May I now turn to the briefing schedule. May I recapitulate the briefing schedule now. The Prosecution filed its notice of appeal in this case on the 31st of December, 2007, and submitted its appeal brief on 30 January 2008. I recall the Prosecution's appeal is limited to sentencing. The Defence notice of appeal was filed on 11 January 2008. In February, the Defence filed a motion seeking an extension of time for the filing of the Defence appeal and Respondent's brief on the basis that Mr. Milosevic had not yet received the official B/C/S translation of the trial judgement. And on the 20th of February, I issued a decision, as the Appeal Judge, granting a motion and ordering the Defence to file its appeal brief within 15 days and the Respondent's brief within seven days of the receipt of the translation. As the parties are aware of, I believe, the Appeal Chamber has been advised by the Registry that the B/C/S translation of the judgement will be available no later than the 1st of August, 2008, so we expect -- the Appeal Chamber expects to receive the appeal brief of the Defence and the Respondent's brief of the Defence within the month of August, within the deadlines as indicated in the decision I issued on 20 February 2008. Now, this is just on the briefing schedule. Is there any issue the parties want to raise as to the briefing schedule or any other issue that they want to raise on this appeal at this point of time? Mr. Tapuskovic, or maybe the Prosecutor first. Or as you wish. I have no problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEWIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution has nothing which it wishes to raise at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: I thank you. The Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I wish to raise an issue which is of crucial importance for the Defence, though I don't want to use strong words. I have your decision, issued on the date you said it would be issued, and you approved a time period of 15 days for Mr. Milosevic to submit his appeal brief. This is to be submitted within 15 days of his receipt of the official translation of the trial judgement. You stated that although Mr. Milosevic's Defence counsel should already be working on their submissions, and this is quite valid because we are in fact already working on this, however I have to raise a point concerning language. We had to study the documents in English, although we are both lawyers who used exclusively French in the course of the proceedings, and we are slightly handicapped by this. But, of course, this is not an obstacle for us to do our work conscientiously every day. We are doing our best to state our appeal in as few words as possible, and at present we don't need to ask for permission to submit a lengthier brief. However, the 15-day period approved by you seems to us to be too short. The judgement is over 300 pages long. In fact, it's 326 pages long. It concerns a large number of incidents, each one of which requires a separate and detailed analysis in order to draw attention to all the points the Appeals Chamber should take into consideration. We therefore feel that this 15-day time period is very short. The accused needs at least 10 days to read and study the judgement for him to give us any suggestions, and of course we must respect his suggestions and deal with them in our appeal brief. You know that the Prosecutor was very magnanimous and agreed with 40 days, which is in harmony with some other decisions issued by this Chamber. For example, in the Prosecutor versus Milan Mrksic, IT-95-13/1-A, and Lemaj, IT-03-66-A. Therefore, we feel it would be highly justified for this 15-day period to be extended within the framework applied in previous cases. In view of the characteristics of the judgement, its voluminousness, the number of incidents it encompasses, and in view of the fact that the Prosecutor did not object, I believe that this is something Your Honour should reconsider.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you. May I ask the Prosecution for their reaction.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEWIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, as my learned friend from the Defence has pointed out, in the Prosecutor's request for the Defence's request for an extension, we did submit that we were of the opinion that between 50 and 40 days would be a fair period of time for the appeals brief and between 7 and 15 days for the response brief, and we stand by that. We have nothing to add.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, let me consider the decision in light of the practice of the Appeals Chamber, which was derogated from in this case and in the Mrksic case, as correctly the Defence is pointing out. The practice of this Appeal Chamber is not to grant all the time that has been granted in this case. The practice of the Appeal Chamber is to keep in this case the briefing schedule as it is in the Rules, allowing when the translation is made available to the party, that party to come with a motion to add something if that is necessary. So I believe the parties have been given -- the Defence has been given already more time than it is granted normally to a Defence in cases of this kind. I know that the Mrksic case went in another direction, but this is not the precedent I intended to follow. Indeed, when I decided in February, my option was either to follow the -- either to follow the practice of the Appeals Chamber, and that would have been to leave undisturbed the briefing schedule, allowing later in August, when the judgement would become available in B/C/S, the Defence to add something to the brief as already submitted in February or March or to decide to grant more time, as I have done, and delay the whole appeal -- the whole appeal brief to August. So in this situation, I am of the view that the Defence has already been given more time than is usually given to prepare its Defence, to prepare the brief, and so I'm not prepared to change my decision of 20th February.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may. Your Honour, I respect your position in every way. However, I do need to ask myself one thing, as Mr. Milosevic's Defence counsel. We are to meet the requirements of justice in relation to Milosevic. The judgement runs into 326 pages. What can he possibly be expected to do over such a short time? He's expected to read the judgement in its entirety. We're not spending all of our time in The Hague. I'm spending most of my time in Belgrade and my colleague in Paris. He will take at least 10 days to read the judgement in its entirety. I assume it should be necessary for us to have sufficient time to at least confer with him so that we can hear him on any suggestions that he might have. This way will be impossible. We have to start working on our appellate brief -- or rather his appellate brief on the very first day after he has received the translation. Once we make it to The Hague, once he's read it, I think 15 days is too short a time for us to communicate effectively to know what his suggestions might be. If we spend several days talking over the phone, it might take more than just several days. We should sit down to it with him, and all of this is despite our best efforts, efforts that we are making already. This is a situation which makes it very difficult for us to approach our task in a conscientious manner. I move that this decision be subjected to another review so that we may perhaps be granted a little more time to sit down with our client and consider any suggestions that he might raise, having read the translation of the judgement in its entirety. That is why I asked for your understanding, Your Honour, in terms of perhaps extending this deadline that the Prosecution, too, has agreed to. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: I thank you, but for the reasons that I have already explained, I'm not prepared to change the briefing schedule as set in the decision of 20 February 2008. If, after the brief has been submitted, for any reason the Defence believes it has to bring a motion showing good cause from bringing additional elements, that motion will be considered by the Appeal Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MS. LEWIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: This is my decision today. Are there any other issues that the parties want to raise at this point? The Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. LEWIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, nothing for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: I thank you. Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not for the time being, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: I thank you. Well, I believe this concludes our business today. I thank the parties for their attendance, and I call the proceedings to a close. The status conference is adjourned.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the status conference concluded at
